identity.name: GALLANTT ISPAT LIMITED
identity.industry: Long Steel / Integrated TMT & Upstream Mining

summary.oneLiner: Gallantt Ispat reported steady FY26 consolidation with improved EBITDA/ton (INR 8,785) and a net-cash balance sheet, setting the stage for a structural re-rating as its INR 3,000 crore capex program (capacity expansion + captive mines) commissions between H2 FY27 and FY28 to drive volume growth and ~INR 2,000/ton cost savings.

one-line thesis: Gallantt Ispat reported steady FY26 consolidation with improved EBITDA/ton (INR 8,785) and a net-cash balance sheet, setting the stage for a structural re-rating as its INR 3,000 crore capex program (capacity expansion + captive mines) commissions between H2 FY27 and FY28 to drive volume growth and ~INR 2,000/ton cost savings.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 4,419 Cr (+3.95% YoY); EBITDA: INR 776 Cr (17.6% margin, +INR 485/ton YoY); PAT: INR 484 Cr (10.8% margin); Order Book: Not disclosed (spot-driven TMT sales); Net Debt: Negative (Net Cash ~INR 360 Cr); One-offs: Significant inter-corporate deposits (INR 294-297 Cr) earning 12% interest classified as loans.
guidance: Revenue: Target INR 5,300-5,400 Cr post-expansion; Margin: Target ~20% EBITDA margin upon mine integration; Order Inflow: Driven by 25% regional market share in UP/Gujarat; Capex/Commissioning: INR 1,200 Cr steel expansion (H2 FY27), INR 300 Cr solar (FY27), INR 1,500 Cr mines (FY28).
order book & pipeline: Sales volume FY26: 766 KT TMT, 81 KT Billet, 125 KT Sponge Iron, 49 KT Pellets. No formal order book disclosed; business operates on spot/short-term contracts with strong regional pricing power.
segment / subsidiary detail: FY26 Production: Pellets 819 KT, Sponge Iron 915 KT, Billet 883 KT, TMT 788 KT. Q4 FY26 Production: Pellets 222 KT, Sponge Iron 245 KT, Billet 235 KT, TMT 210 KT. Internal consumption of semi-finished goods increasing to capture value add.
growth verticals / optionality: Phase 1: Capacity scale-up from 1.0 MTPA to 1.3 MTPA (H2 FY27). Phase 2: Captive mine commissioning (FY28) unlocking INR 2,000/ton EBITDA benefit. Phase 3: Potential medium-term plan announcement in Q2 FY27 for further scale/acquisitions.
margins & cost dynamics: FY26 EBITDA/ton improved to INR 8,785 (vs INR 8,300 in FY25) despite softer realizations. Raw material cost held steady at 72% of net realization. Future margin expansion to ~20% driven by captive mines (INR 2,000/ton saving) and solar power (INR 30-40 Cr annual saving).
capex / expansion: Total program INR 3,000 Cr: INR 1,200 Cr for steel capacity expansion (ongoing, H2 FY27 completion); INR 300 Cr for 78 MW solar (18 MW Gujarat, 60 MW UP, FY27 completion); INR 1,500 Cr for 4 captive mines (Rajasthan/UP, target FY28). FY26 actual spend INR 320 Cr.
capital allocation: 100% of past 5-year capex (INR 1,200 Cr) funded via internal accruals. Current surplus cash (INR 800 Cr gross, INR 360 Cr net) deployed in short-term inter-corporate deposits at 12%. Future capex primarily internal accruals, no equity raise planned for current INR 3,000 Cr program.
risks & watch-items: Execution risk on aggressive FY28 mine commissioning timeline; Regulatory delays in mine approvals; Volatility in iron ore/coal prices before captive supply kicks in; Implementation challenges of large-scale capex.
management quality / tone: Confident, disciplined, and transparent. Emphasis on 'capital discipline' (net cash), 'integration depth', and 'structural demand'. First-ever earnings call signaled a shift towards greater investor engagement.
non-obvious takeaways: Company earns ~12% risk-adjusted returns on temporary cash surplus via inter-corporate loans, effectively subsidizing capex costs. Regional dominance (25% share) in UP/Gujarat allows pricing premium over peers, insulating from national price wars.

themes.title: Metals & mining cycle - steel, aluminium, critical minerals
themes.need: Domestic demand growth, safeguard duties and an India capacity-expansion wave lift integrated metals while critical-mineral security gains policy support. TATASTEEL targets 45-50 MT India (FY26 India EBITDA INR34,272cr at 24% margin) with a +INR6,000/t 1QFY27 realisation uplift; JINDALSTEL/SAIL/JSWSTEEL-tier on steel; HINDALCO/NALCO on aluminium; HINDZINC on zinc (Q1FY27 all-time-record EBITDA INR8,074cr +109% YoY on a record-low zinc cost-of-production USD851/t, though CEO Arun Misra hands over to ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash 1-Aug-2026 and a new Gundlupet REE/Yttrium critical-minerals block won this quarter is a 2031-32-dated option, not near-term); NMDC/COALINDIA/LLOYDSME/SARDAEN on iron-ore/coal/integrated mining. Q1FY27 also quantified the export-side shock and the downstream escape from it: JINDALSAW's consolidated PAT fell 78% YoY to INR 91cr on +9% revenue because the Strait-of-Hormuz blockade suspended ALL India-origin MENA export shipments from March 2026, holding utilisation at ~60-65%; SHYAMMETL took the other route, posting INR 5,455cr revenue (+23.3%) at a multi-quarter-high 14.9% EBITDA margin with aluminium EBITDA/t +52% YoY and specialty alloys near 20.5% margin, self-funding ~INR 9,580cr of balance capex with no debt.
themes.driver: Steel price/realisation uplift into Q1; safeguard-duty support; Hormuz reopening for line-pipe exports; value-added/downstream mix; iron-ore + critical-mineral volume ramp.
